LORENA NATIVIDAD-BORJA Sangguniang Panlungsod Member Valenzuela City Dear SP Member Borja: This pertains to your letter seeking our legal opinion on the scope of the authority of the Committee on Ethics, Good Government and Public Accountability of that sanggunian regarding matters involving disciplinary cases against appointive barangay officials. In reply thereto, please allow us to restate the pertinent provisions of the Local Government Code related to your query, to wit: "SEC. 61. Form and Filing Of Administrative Complaints.- A verified complaint against any erring local elective official shall be prepared as follows: xxx xxx xxx (c) A complaint against any_ elective barangay official shall be filed before the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concerned whose decision shall be final and executory." (underlining ours) "SEC. 87. Disciplinary Jurisdiction.- Except as otherwise provided by law, the local chief executive may impose the penalty of removal from service, demotion in rank, suspension for not more than one (1) year without pay, fine in an amount not exceeding six (6) months' salary, or reprimand and otherwise discipline subordinate officials and employees under his jurisdiction. If the penalty imposed is suspension without pay for not more than thirty (30) days, his decision shali be final. If the penalty imposed is heavier than suspension of thirty (30) days, the

-2- decision shall be to the Civil Service Commission, which shall decide the appeal Within thirty (30) days from receipt thereof." From the foregoing,l it is crystal clear that the disciplinary authority of the Sangguniang Parqunésod over barangay officials extends only to elective barangay officials.. The Sangguniang Panlungsod can only exercise that power which is conferred by Jaw or necessarily implied therefrom. Accordingly, since the disciplinary jurisdiction vested unto the Sangguniang ertains only to elective barangay officials, then, it cannot exercise disciplinary authority over appointive barangay officials, such as barangay treasurer; barangay secretary, tanods, etc. An administrative c se against an appointive barangay official is governed by another fecffon of the same Code, which is Section 87 as aforequoted. In a barangay, ocaJ Chief Executive is the Punong Barangay. Therefore, based on Secti n 87 of the Local Government Code and the suppletory application t e Civil Service laws, the Punong Barangay is the disciplinary authority over ppointive barangay officials, such as barangay treasurers, barangay secret ries, barangay tanods, etc. Hope we have enightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, MEL O P. ROSALES ctin Secreta LOCAL REPtnw;, SILG05-007216 copy furnished: Director Rodolfo S. Feraren DILG-NCR LMP Building, Ermin Garci St' Cubao, Quezon City
